newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends down, hovers near support.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends down, hovers near support.

text.p: * Value turnover above average at 3.2 billion pesos
The Manila share index finished down on Monday as thirdliner issues continued to divert funds away from blue chips, traders said.
"Market is consolidating as there's nothing directional in the short-term although long-term there is confidence among investors," Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities said.
The main index dipped at the close by 7.46 points, or 0.22 percent, to 3,314.84.

Some 60 percent of the day's trade was on speculative issues and a 30-point drop in the index in late trade was stymied by gains of index-linked stocks Ayala Corp A and Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co at close, traders said.
Bucking the trend of most blue chips, Ayala Corp A closed one peso up, or four percent, at 26 pesos while Metrobank ended ten pesos higher, or 1.36 percent, at 740 pesos.

Traders said news that members of the ruling party were pushing for changes in the constitution to enable an extension of the six-year term of the presidency was used by some investors as an excuse to stay in the sidelines or sell.

"If you see the executive department and Congress embroiled in a debate on charter changes, then they will be focusing their energies on politics to the detriment of economic bills," said Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president for institutional sales at Philippine Asia Equity.
The Dow Jones' and PLDT's drop in New York also helped in pulling down the index, brokers said.
Decliners outnumbered gainers 77 to 60 with 62 issues unchanged. Only the oil, finance and mining issues closed up.

Philippine Asia Equity's Lozada added: "Local punters are playing up speculative issues and this may be a pre-cursor of a big drop in the market or that bigger issues are just pausing on lack of corporate news."
"We will likely see the same sideways trading on Tuesday as most of the corporate earnings of big companies are out," Rudsend Alpay, assistant vice-president at Lippo Securities predicted.
